Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Why Arabic, and is a translation enough for me?

Each messenger came in his people's tongue, to be clear. What a translation carries, and what it loses.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِۦ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ ۖ فَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allāh sends astray [thereby] whom He wills[649] and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

Translator's notes

[649] i.e., those who refuse His guidance.

Quran · Ibrahim 14:4

A sender who wants a message to arrive must speak in what people understand. So the verse makes the rule general: every messenger in the tongue of his people, and the reason is to make things clear to them. Language here is about arrival, and not about rank. Muhammad was an Arab among Arabs, so the book came in Arabic, as other messengers spoke their people's tongues. The question left is how it reaches everyone else.

A question for you

From the verse, what do you take the choice of Arabic to mean?

If you sayIt was the language of the first hearers.
ThenThat is the reason the verse gives: clarity for them.
If you sayThat Arabic is the best language.
ThenSome people say so, but the verse does not. 30:22 counts the variety of tongues as a sign.
If you sayI feel left out.
ThenAn understandable feeling, and the next verse starts from an objection close to it.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَـٰهُ قُرْءَانًا أَعْجَمِيًّا لَّقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا فُصِّلَتْ ءَايَـٰتُهُۥٓ ۖ ءَا۬عْجَمِىٌّ وَعَرَبِىٌّ ۗ قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ هُدًى وَشِفَآءٌ ۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى ۚ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِن مَّكَانٍۭ بَعِيدٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And if We had made it a foreign [i.e., non-Arabic] Qur’ān, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail [in our language]? Is it a foreign [recitation] and an Arab [messenger]?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and cure." And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.[1398]

Translator's notes

[1398] For all practical purposes, since they neither hear nor understand.

Quran · Fussilat 41:44

Some people objected to the language itself, and the verse quotes the objection: had it come in a foreign tongue they would have said, why are its verses not made clear? An objection can be raised in any language. Then the verse moves the question deeper: for those who believe it is guidance and healing. In the end the issue is more than language. It is how a heart receives it.

A question for you

Which matters more to you in reading a sacred text?

If you sayUnderstanding the meaning.
ThenThen you share the verses' own reason: clarity.
If you sayHearing the original.
ThenThat is what no translation gives. Try listening to the recitation, even without understanding it.
If you sayFeeling close.
ThenThere is another question for that, on prayer in your own language.

Part 3 of 3

﴿إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ قُرْءَٰنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān[583] that you might understand.

Translator's notes

[583] i.e., revealed in the Arabic language.

Quran · Yusuf 12:2

﴿وَمِنْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ خَلْقُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱخْتِلَـٰفُ أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَأَلْوَٰنِكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَـٰتٍ لِّلْعَـٰلِمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:22

Translation

Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?

Original · Hebrew

הֲֽ֝לֹא־בַ֭בֶּטֶן עֹשֵׂ֣נִי עָשָׂ֑הוּ וַ֝יְכֻנֶ֗נּוּ בָּרֶ֥חֶם אֶחָֽד׃

Job · 31:15

World English Bible

If the purpose of the Arabic is that you may understand, then one who grasps a verse's meaning through a translation has reached a real part of that purpose. A translation is not the Quran itself. It is a human reading that carries meaning and loses sound and structure. So the Arabic stays the reference, and this app shows it beside every translation. The second verse counts the variety of tongues among God's signs.

A question for you

How would you describe a translation after reading this?

If you sayA bridge to the meaning.
ThenThat is how this app uses one, with the original beside it.
If you sayIt is not the Quran.
ThenThat is the distinction scholars keep, and it does not stop you from learning through one.
If you sayI would like to learn Arabic.
ThenA beautiful wish. Each Step shows a few words you can start with.

Your reflection

What word do you wish you could know in its original sense?
